references.text: Moses prophesied that God would raise up a prophet like himself, and the people should listen to him—'you shall listen to him'—which is directly reflected in the words 'αὐτοῦ ἀκούετε' (listen to him).
The psalm declares, 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you,' which forms the background for the divine declaration from the cloud, 'This is my Son.'

The Lord's servant is referred to as the chosen one: 'my servant whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom my soul delights.' The word 'ὁ ἐκλελεγμένος' (the chosen one) in Luke 9:35 has a strong connection to this passage from Isaiah.
At Jesus' baptism, a similar voice sounded from heaven: 'This is my beloved Son; with him I am well pleased.' This is a parallel divine proclamation.
Matthew's parallel account of the transfiguration on the mountain, where the voice from the cloud says, 'This is my beloved Son; with him I am well pleased. Listen to him!'
Mark's parallel account of the transfiguration, where the voice from the cloud says, 'This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!'
Peter testifies that he heard the voice from heaven on the holy mountain: 'This is my beloved Son; with him I am well pleased.' This confirms the account of the transfiguration.
The Lord speaks about his chosen servant Israel/Jacob, but prophetically points to the chosen Messiah. The term 'chosen' is linked to Luke 9:35.
John the Baptist testifies: 'I have seen it and have testified that this is the Son of God.' Here, the identity of the Son of God is confirmed just as in the transfiguration scene.
God says he will put his words in the prophet's mouth, and whoever does not listen to those words shall be held accountable. This supports the command 'listen to him' in Luke 9:35.
